This lesson teaches **to like / love** (حب) and **to want** (عايز), plus the small machinery you need to talk about *whose* thing it is and *which* thing: possessive endings and the words for "this / that". Tap any sentence to reveal its franco and English.

## How it works

**حب is a doubled verb.** Its root ح-ب-ب has a repeated last letter, so the present keeps the doubled *bb*: **بحب (ba7ebb)** = "I like / I love". Egyptian uses the one verb for both *like* and *love*. Future is just **ها +** the stem: *ha7ebb*.

**Negation wraps the verb in ما...ش.** "I don't like" = **مبحبش (maba7ebbesh)** — *ma-* before, *-sh* after. Same pattern for any person: *mabit7ebbesh* ("you don't like").

**عايز ("want") is not a normal verb** — it's an adjective-like word that *agrees* with the speaker and takes no بـ: **عايز (3ayez)** for a man, **عايزة (3ayza)** for a woman, **عايزين (3ayzeen)** for plural. Negative: *mesh 3ayez*.

**"This / that" comes after the noun, and the noun takes the article.** *el-2amis da* = "this shirt", *el-geeba di* = "this skirt". The demonstrative agrees: **ده (da)** masculine, **دي (di)** feminine, **دول (dol)** plural. Everyday Egyptian uses these for both *this* and *that*; for "that one by you / over there" you may hear **دياك (dyyak)**, but ده/دي usually cover both.

## Possessive endings

Glued onto the end of the noun. A feminine noun ending in ة slips in a **‑t‑** first (*gezma* → *gezmet‑ak*).

| Ending - franco | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ـي - ‑i | my |
| ـك - ‑ak (m.) / ‑ek (f.) | your |
| ـه - ‑o | his |
| ـها - ‑ha | her |
| ـنا - ‑na | our |
| ـكو - ‑ko | your (pl.) |
| ـهم - ‑hom | their |

</details>

<details class="frase">

<span class="fr">ana maba7ebbesh gezmetak di</span>

</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>هو بيحب جاكيتنا دا</summary>
<span class="fr">huwwa biy7ebb gaketna da</span>
<span class="en">he likes our jacket</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>إحنا بنحب الفستان ده</summary>
<span class="fr">e7na bin7ebb el-fustan da</span>
<span class="en">we like this dress</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>إنتِ بتحبي الجيبة دي</summary>
<span class="fr">inti bit7ebbi el-geeba di</span>
<span class="en">you (f.) like this skirt</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا مبحبش النضارة دي</summary>
<span class="fr">ana maba7ebbesh el-naddara di</span>
<span class="en">I don't like these glasses</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>إنت بتحب البلوزة دياك</summary>
<span class="fr">inta bit7ebb el-boloza dyyak</span>
<span class="en">you (m.) like that blouse by you</span>
</details>

## To like / love — حب — 7abb

**Root:** ح-ب-ب (7-b-b) — doubled verb. Future: ها + stem (*ana ha7ebb, huwwa hay7ebb*).

| Pronoun | Present |
|---|---|
| أنا - ana | بحب - ba7ebb |
| إنت - inta | بتحب - bit7ebb |
| إنتِ - inti | بتحبي - bit7ebbi |
| هو - huwwa | بيحب - biy7ebb |
| هي - hiyya | بتحب - bit7ebb |
| إحنا - e7na | بنحب - bin7ebb |
| إنتو - intu | بتحبوا - bit7ebbu |
| هم - humma | بيحبوا - biy7ebbu |

**Negation (ما...ش):** *maba7ebbesh* (I don't like), *mabit7ebbesh* (you don't like), *mabiy7ebbesh* (he doesn't like).

## To want — عايز — 3ayez

Not conjugated — it just agrees in gender and number.

| Form - franco | Used by |
|---|---|
| عايز - 3ayez | a man |
| عايزة - 3ayza | a woman |
| عايزين - 3ayzeen | plural |

**Negation:** *mesh 3ayez / mesh 3ayza* (I don't want).

## Clothing

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| قميص - 2amis (m.) | shirt |
| تيشيرت - tee-shirt (m.) | t-shirt |
| بنطلون - bantalon (m.) | trousers |
| جاكيت - gaket (m.) | jacket |
| فستان - fustan (m.) | dress |
| جيبة - geeba (f.) | skirt |
| بلوزة - boloza (f.) | blouse |
| جزمة - gezma (f.) | shoes |
| نضارة - naddara (f.) | glasses |
| طرحة - tar7a (f.) | headscarf |

## Dialogue: at the shop

Omar is shopping; Dina helps.

<span class="rotulo">دينا — Dina</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>بتحب القميص ده؟</summary>
<span class="fr">bit7ebb el-2amis da?</span>
<span class="en">Do you like this shirt?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">عمر — Omar</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>أيوة، بحبه قوي</summary>
<span class="fr">aywa, ba7ebbo 2awi</span>
<span class="en">Yes, I like it a lot</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">دينا — Dina</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>وعايز إيه كمان؟</summary>
<span class="fr">we 3ayez eh kaman?</span>
<span class="en">And what else do you want?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">عمر — Omar</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>عايز الجاكيت ده لأخويا</summary>
<span class="fr">3ayez el-gaket da le-a5oya</span>
<span class="en">I want this jacket for my brother</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">دينا — Dina</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>والجزمة دي؟</summary>
<span class="fr">wel-gezma di?</span>
<span class="en">And these shoes?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">عمر — Omar</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>لأ، دي مش حلوة</summary>
<span class="fr">la2, di mesh 7elwa</span>
<span class="en">No, they're not nice</span>
</details>
